title: JOINT STUDY ON LONG-TERM SPACE-BASED EARTH OBSERVATION TECHNOLOGY ROADMAPS
description: This study is a joint initiative of ESA through its ERS EO Programme, Element 1 and the European Defence Agency (EDA) aimed at identifying strategic and technology gaps in defence-related Earth Observation and defining recommendations for a subsequent critical EOtechnology development roadmap towards 2040 and beyond. The study will identify key research and development priorities supporting long-term European space-based Earth Observation capabilities for defence applications, while maximising synergies between ESA and EDA activities in this field. ESA will be responsible for conducting the tender process in close coordination with EDA.

title: GLOBAL VALUE-ADDING PLATFORM PRODUCTION CAPACITY: ENERGY ASSET MAPPING, MONITORING AND ATTRIBUTION
description: Spatially explicit and timely information on energy system infrastructure and facilities (hereafter referred to as energy assets) is an essential input to energy demand and supply planning and related applications. The use of Earth Observation (EO) to map and monitor energy assets has previously been demonstrated, for example, for wind turbines or utility-scale photovoltaics (PV). Existing EOobservational capacities together with advanced analytical methods have the potential to advance the utility of EO for energy assetmonitoring. Moreover, such monitoring approaches can now be devised to generate information at continental to global scale and in arepeatable manner. The International Energy Agency (IEA) is an intergovernmental organisation that analyses the global energy sectorand provides authoritative analysis and data to support policymaking worldwide. This makes the IEA a strategic stakeholder for the ESA EO Programmes to further advance and mature related EO capabilities for the energy sector and other downstream applications. This ITT aims to develop an EO value-adding capacity to detect, monitor and characterise selected energy assets at global scale and create a set of dedicated, quality-controlled geospatial products. The IEA has engaged with ESA in the context of this ITT in a co-creation approach, contributing to the definition of objectives and requirements, and will support the evaluation and valorisation of the resulting value-added products. The specific objectives of this ITT are to (1) detect and map selected categories of energyassets globally, (2) employ a monitoring approach to characterise their operational characteristics, (3) optimise a cloud-based, value-adding production system to facilitate cost efficient future updates of the targeted products. The list of targeted energy assets includes wind turbines, large-scale PV power plants, hyperscale AI data centres and open-pit mining operations. The required detection system will employ a two-scale approach, first using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data for global mapping and detection, then secondly using higher-resolution data to confirm detections. The subsequent monitoring of assets' operational characteristics shall employmultimodal EO observations and utilise time series signals to infer relevant attributes. Rigorous quality control and validation ofthe resulting products is a key part of the activity. The resulting value-adding production capacity will be deployed on a public European EO cloud computing platform and shall enable future product updates on-demand in a computationally and cost-efficient mannerand shall be offered on a commercial basis.

title: ATMOSPHERIC CHANNEL MODEL FOR EO DATA DOWNLINK USING MULTIPLE SATELLITES AND GROUND STATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a propagation channel model for the design and simulation of the EO data download at Ka- and Q-band for satellite constellations and a network of ground stations.Description: The design and optimisation of the radio link at Ka and Q band for the download of scientific data from an EO mission or a constellation requires the knowledge of the dynamic properties of the atmospheric radio channel over the sky during a pass. This is needed for the evaluation of the achievable data throughput and for the design of adaptive techniques like adaptive coding and modulation (ACM). The evolution of EO observation systems from a single satellite to a train or a constellation of different spacecrafts requires also the knowledge of the spatial and temporal characteristics of the atmospheric channel during the passes of EO satellites. In addition, due to the large amount of data volume it could be neededto perform the data download from a spacecraft by using sequentially more than one ground station during the orbit. Therefore, the channel model shall consider also this configuration in its assumptions and parametrisations. Current channel models for EO data downlink have been originally developed for the case of a satellite using a single station, so they need to be updated to take into account the temporal and spatial correlation of atmospheric propagation effects during a satellite pass and over the regions crossed during an orbit. These models have not been validated using experimental data, because of the lack of propagation measurements at Ka band or above. In the meantime new non-geostationary (NGSO) constellations data have been collected and can be used for model testing.This activity aims at developing a propagation channel model for the design and simulation of the data download of EO data at 26 and 40 GHz for the cases of : - A ground station antenna tracking at the same time the passes of several EO satellites - An EO satellite completing the download of observations, and using more than one ground station during its orbit to do so. The model shall be validated using existing data from propagation campaigns at Ka band or above using satellites in non-geostationary (i.e. LEO or MEO). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - State-of-the-art review of system requirements, channel models and NGSO propagationmeasurements, model development and testing plan - Development of channel model and preparation for testing - Model testing with experimental NGSO propagation data - Application of the new model to system test-cases - Test-case analysesDeliverables: Report, SoftwareProcurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SME  RD organisations, preferably in cooperation. For additional informationplease go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: T708-900SY ADVANCING GREENER MANUFACTURING, ASSEMBLY, INTEGRATION AND TEST PROCESSES (EXPRO+)
description: Reducing environmental impacts is now required for ESA space systems under the ESA Ecodesign Policy endorsed in October 2025, shifting the focus from impact assessment to practical ecodesign solutions implementation supporting the ESA Green Agenda 2030 greenhouse gas reduction targets.  Space systems involve specific manufacturing processes and energy-intensive testing. Previous ESA work led to the ESA Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) Database, already used by European industry. However, Manufacturing, Assembly, Integration and Test (MAIT) activities remain insufficiently covered in mission LCAs, limiting assessment reliability, especially in early phases.  This activity will therefore analyse MAIT processes, develop validated datasets for the ESA LCA Database, and identify greener technologies to reduce future mission impacts. It will build on previous TDE T824-801SY on greener MAIT processes, but also onESA LCA Database activities, and generic databases such as ecoinvent.
